L14: - **Load before / after:** other-process CPU averaged 1.67% / 1.22% over 5-second windows. Available RAM was 79,950,389,248 / 79,880,933,376 bytes. The busiest processes were Task Manager and short-lived Claude processes; no other process exceeded 0.6% machine CPU in either sample.
L19: - **Configuration:** the scale bench's M2-40 equilibrium configuration, `N ∈ {25k, 50k, 100k, 150k, 200k, 300k, 400k, 500k, 750k, 1M}`, `K=N/200`, `k=8`, `p_local=0.5`, seed `81985529216486895`, replicate `7`.
L20: - **Sampling:** two warmups and 15 timed samples per cell; each sample ran three consecutive days with scratch reuse. The reported profile medians and MADs use 45 timed day observations. Every sample restarts from the same day-0 checkpoint; initialization and graph/projection setup are outside phase timers.
L21: - **Profile validity:** the bench-only `ManualProfile::step` was compared on every day to `run_m3_storage_days`: `M3DayOutcome` and canonical State hash matched. The reversed-slot checks separately compared State, Metrics, and Events digests.
L118: ### Estimated bytes touched per phase/day
L120: These are code-derived logical field and scratch estimates, not hardware memory-controller counters. At 1M, `N=1,000,000`, `K=5,000`, `k=8`; `A` is alive agents, `W` work intents, `T` targeted intents, `E` keyed Phase 6B entries, `D` deaths, and `R` staged events. Sorting, hash-table bucket traffic, cache-line overfetch, and repeated comparison loads add traffic beyond the compulsory-field estimates.
L122: | Phase | Estimated compulsory field traffic | Index, projection, scratch, and variable work |
L124: | P1 | `8K` B (resource `f32` read + write; about 40 KB) | Settlement vector only; no agent columns. |
L125: | P2 | `17N` B (alive 1, health 4 and food 4 read; health and food 8 written; about 17 MB) | Sequential column scan; no per-agent allocation. |
L126: | P3 | `25N` B read + `24A` B feature output (about 49 MB) | Dense GroupId lookup vector, duplicate flags, and scarcity values are `O(K)`; the measured 0..K−1 IDs use direct lookup. Sparse/non-dense IDs use the sorted fallback. `AgentFeatures` output sort remains. |
L127: | P4 action | About `53A` B (feature 24, AgentId 4, alive/health 5, cooperation/aggression/risk 12, choice output about 8; about 53 MB) | `features` and `choices` vectors are `O(N)`; choices are sorted by AgentId. |
L128: | P4 intent | About `25N` B base reads + `24N` B Intent output (about 49 MB) | For `T` targeted initiators, projected-row offsets add about `16T` B; each of `kT` neighbor visits reads an 8-byte slot plus AgentId/alive/health/food (about 21 bytes). At `k=8`, this is approximately `184T` B plus the persistent projection (`72N` B at 64-bit slots, about 72 MB) and a `k`-sized AgentId candidate scratch. |
L129: | P5 | About `24N` B to read intents and `24N` B to move them into group buckets (about 48 MB) | Reusable GroupId→bucket HashMap and per-group vectors; `K` partition records sorted by GroupId. Per-group Vec storage is allocated as groups are drained and rebuilt. |
L130: | P6A | About `24N` B intent traversal plus roughly `45W` B of worker validation/planning/commit fields | `slot_of` HashMap gathers; settlement index `O(K)`; per-group Work lists sort to AgentId order, with `Σ W_g log W_g ≤ W log W`. |
L131: | P6B | About `24T` B intent reads | `slot_of` lookups; validated/keyed records are about 48 B each. Their reusable buffers are reserved to population capacity (`N`) in the M3 run context; live entries are `T`/`E`. Global `E log E` sort, then live-state gathers and food updates. |

Full-tick M3P medians were roughly 179–182 ms at 100k; the equal-live M3 path was about 31.6 ms/tick at the day-400 checkpoint.

L18: The workload is the accepted M3-08 sustained configuration: M2-40 food-supply and decision-policy changes, M3P `k=8`, `p_local=0.5`, birth probability `0.0001`, unlimited births, and compaction interval 50 days. Measurements used `N=10,000, K=50` and `N=100,000, K=500`, master seed `81985529216486895`, and replicate `7`. Configuration details are in [M3-08 Population Dynamics](M3_08_POPULATION_DYNAMICS.md).
L20: The temporary full-tick command was `cargo run --release -p sim-model --example m3p_09_measure`. It used two paired trajectories per population, with days 0–99 as an unmeasured trajectory warm-up and executed days 100–400 measured. Serial and incremental one-day calls were interleaved in alternating order from the same initial configuration. Each call reused its runner context and scratch. Metrics and events were enabled; snapshots were disabled. Initialization, graph creation, and context creation were outside the timer. Every paired daily `M3pDayOutcome` was compared exactly, and final State hashes matched after the timed horizon. The runner does not request a State digest on each normal tick; the final hash check was outside the timer, so the dirty CSR hash stayed deferred during normal execution. Each run reports the median ± MAD across 301 day samples, separated into 294 normal days and seven compaction days.
L22: The equal-live comparison used the day-400 M3P checkpoint. It used two warm-ups, 11 timed samples, three consecutive days per sample, with contexts constructed before timing and metrics/events enabled. The M3 profile used the same live M3P agent records and settlement state. Baseline and incremental M3P outcomes matched for every sample.
L24: Per-phase and Phase 9b substage timings came from temporary `Instant` hooks in the runner and Phase 9b planner, enabled only for one release profile run per population with `cargo run --release -p sim-model --example m3p_09_measure -- phase`. The hooks printed timing records and were removed afterward. These timings are secondary, include hook/printing overhead, and are not additive. Full-tick timings above were collected with profiling disabled. The incremental M3P/serial M3 ratio is measured separately with two warm-ups and 11 timed samples of three consecutive days each; each runner context is built outside its sample timer.
L102: **Measured facts:** at 100k, the normal-day Phase 9b total moved from about 114 ms in the M3-08 apply-plus-projection measurements to about 22 ms in the incremental profile. The full tick moved from the M3-08 serial medians around 179–181 ms to paired incremental medians around 74–75 ms. The equal-live M3P/M3 ratio moved from 5.23× in M3-08 to 2.58× for the incremental path in this run. On compaction days the incremental path still runs the canonical rebuild; the hook-timed 100k Phase 9b total was about 117 ms.

L18: The workload is the accepted M3-08 sustained configuration: M2-40 food-supply and decision-policy changes, M3P `k=8`, `p_local=0.5`, birth probability `0.0001`, unlimited births, and compaction interval 50 days. Measurements used `N=10,000, K=50` and `N=100,000, K=500`, master seed `81985529216486895`, and replicate `7`. Configuration details are in [M3-08 Population Dynamics](M3_08_POPULATION_DYNAMICS.md).
L20: The temporary full-tick command was `cargo run --release -p sim-model --example m3p_09_measure`. It used two paired trajectories per population, with days 0–99 as an unmeasured trajectory warm-up and executed days 100–400 measured. Serial and incremental one-day calls were interleaved in alternating order from the same initial configuration. Each call reused its runner context and scratch. Metrics and events were enabled; snapshots were disabled. Initialization, graph creation, and context creation were outside the timer. Every paired daily `M3pDayOutcome` was compared exactly, and final State hashes matched after the timed horizon. The runner does not request a State digest on each normal tick; the final hash check was outside the timer, so the dirty CSR hash stayed deferred during normal execution. Each run reports the median ± MAD across 301 day samples, separated into 294 normal days and seven compaction days.
L22: The equal-live comparison used the day-400 M3P checkpoint. It used two warm-ups, 11 timed samples, three consecutive days per sample, with contexts constructed before timing and metrics/events enabled. The M3 profile used the same live M3P agent records and settlement state. Baseline and incremental M3P outcomes matched for every sample.
L24: Per-phase and Phase 9b substage timings came from temporary `Instant` hooks in the runner and Phase 9b planner, enabled only for one release profile run per population with `cargo run --release -p sim-model --example m3p_09_measure -- phase`. The hooks printed timing records and were removed afterward. These timings are secondary, include hook/printing overhead, and are not additive. Full-tick timings above were collected with profiling disabled. The incremental M3P/serial M3 ratio is measured separately with two warm-ups and 11 timed samples of three consecutive days each; each runner context is built outside its sample timer.
L104: **Inference:** the normal-day gain comes from skipping full CSR reconstruction and projection rebuilding, while compaction cost remains dominated by required full graph cleanup and reconstruction. The residual normal-day Phase 9b time is about 22 ms at 100k. `apply_phase9b_storage_incremental` still materializes storage agents and validates a planning state each day; those scans/copies are candidates for later measurement, not part of this stage. The equal-live comparison and phase-hook values have more run-to-run and instrumentation sensitivity than the uninstrumented paired full-tick result.

L9: The serial M3 storage runner remains the default. The explicit parallel spread path does not help when the active frontier is small. In this measured workload it first beat serial Phase 9c at day-0 frontier sizes of 728 sources for pools 2 and 4, and 852 for pool 6; these are observed workload points, not portable thresholds. Larger frontiers amortized per-level dispatch and merge work. At N=100,000, k=16, max_hops=16, transmit_probability=0.2, the day-0 frontier peaked at 29,753; Phase 9c fell from 208.693 ms serial to 65.283 ms on pool 6. The same workload's three-day whole tick improved by 2.26× interleaved and 2.29× non-interleaved on pool 6.
L15: - **Configuration:** the M3-04 equilibrium preset: M2-40 TOML with `environment.base_metabolic_cost=0.3129`; seed `81985529216486895`; replicate `7`; `K=N/200`; `p_local=0.5`; propagation enabled with `seed_probability=0.002`, `forget_probability=0.02`; `k ∈ {8,16}`, `max_hops ∈ {1,2,4,8,16}`, and `transmit_probability ∈ {0.05,0.2}`. The 40 measured cells are `N ∈ {10,000,100,000}` across that matrix.
L17: - **Pools:** caller-owned pools with `{1,2,4,6}` threads and chunk size `256`; pools were constructed outside the timed region.
L18: - **Whole tick:** public `run_m3prop_storage_days` and `run_m3prop_storage_days_with_parallel_spread`; metrics and events enabled, snapshots disabled. Two warmups and 11 timed samples; each sample runs three consecutive days and averages µs/tick. Every sample starts from the same freshly initialized state; graph, projection, context, and pool construction are outside the timer. Serial/parallel order alternates in the interleaved series; the non-interleaved series runs all serial samples before all parallel samples. Per-day metrics, event digests, and final M3PROP storage State digest are asserted equal.
L19: - **Phase 9c:** the public storage serial and parallel Phase 9c functions were timed separately on the same day-0 post-mortality storage state. Two warmups and 11 samples; fresh propagation state was prepared outside each timed call. Both interleaved and non-interleaved medians are reported. A benchmark-only frontier tracer mirrors the frozen seed/spread coordinates and level barriers; its counts and resulting propagation map are asserted equal to the production serial function.
L20: - **Golden trace:** the committed M3-11 propagation reference fixture was run for 300 days; its daily `levels_used` and `max_frontier_size` are listed below.
L21: - **Noise note:** no process-priority boost or CPU pinning was applied. Other Cargo work, including `cargo-nextest`, was observed running during the measurement. The 100k whole-tick MADs are consequently variable; comparisons are descriptive medians from this run, not portable crossover guarantees.
L23: - **Benchmark wall time:** `2,476.702 s` (`41 min 16.702 s`).
